data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's own countercondition undercuts its absolute claim: if small services are truly minimal (e.g., static sites with no shared runtime dependencies), correlated failures are less likely. But the problem explicitly asks to compare decentralized networks against 'one large service with strictly more total internal redundancy.' A minimal-footprint decentralized network can have fewer correlated failure paths than a large service whose extra redundancy shares common infrastructure layers. SRC_003 asserts decentralized networks are 'systematically more vulnerable' yet cannot explain why a large service with strictly more redundancy is immune to the same shared-dependency critique it levels at small services; a large service also depends on common libraries, cloud providers, and runtime infrastructure. The asymmetry SRC_003 claims is not established.
